text:
Tom: Hey @people-ops — heads up I'm planning a 3-month secondment to London from 2026-05-10 to 2026-08-09 to work with the EU team. Quick Qs: do I need to change my home base in HR, how does the WFH stipend work when I'm abroad, and will payroll/tax withholding change?

Elena: Nice — thanks for flagging, Tom. Short answers: 1) Yes, we need a temporary home-base change recorded for the period. 2) WFH stipend can continue but will be prorated for partial months and may be handled differently if we need a UK payroll cutover. 3) Payroll/tax depends on whether we run UK payroll or keep you on US payroll for the stint — that determines NI and PAYE. Please fill the short secondment form so we can route to payroll & legal: https://intra.redwood.com/hr/secondment-form (fields: name, manager, start_date, end_date, host_country, workstation, benefits-request).

Tom: Thanks Elena. If I keep US payroll for the 3 months, any extra tax filings I should expect?

Anya: Hi — from legal/tax side: 90 days usually doesn't automatically create permanent establishment but it can create personal tax obligations for you (UK statutory residence rules). For a 3-month secondment we often keep people on US payroll but we still need to check with our UK payroll partner about voluntary PAYE withholding vs. you filing self-assessment. Please don't assume no filing is required. I'll loop in payroll.

Miguel: Also curious about benefits — will company health cover and pension continue without gap?

Elena: Benefits: core Redwood benefits remain active (medical enrollment remains as-is) for short secondments; however local reimbursement or top-ups (if you see provider co-pays abroad) may require pre-approval. Pension: if you're US 401(k) it continues, but UK auto-enrolment won't kick in unless we're on UK payroll. We'll note that on the form.

Payroll Bot: Ticket PA-3452 created and assigned to EU-payroll. Estimated SLA: 3 business days for initial review.

Tom: Cool — does WFH stipend need to stop if I'm using a coworking space in London for part of the time?

Elena: No need to stop — WFH stipend is intended to offset recurring home-office costs. If you're transitioning to coworking full-time, we'd treat coworking as an office expense and you'd expense it under Travel/Workspace. For mixed setups we do stipend + expense for occasional coworking days. We'll prorate stipend for the move month.

Anya: One more note: if you plan to bill any UK customers while there, escalate — that affects nexus/PE risk for Redwood. Don't do client-facing contracting changes without PM/legal sign-off.

Tom: Got it. I've submitted the secondment form and attached dates + manager sign-off.

People Ops Bot: Form received. Next steps: (1) People Ops to confirm home-base change request, (2) EU-payroll to advise on withholding and any local payroll setup, (3) Legal to review tax/residence flags. Expected follow-up by 2026-04-02.

Elena: Great — thanks for submitting. We'll confirm the stipend proration and whether we need a UK payroll cutover after EU-payroll reviews. I'll post back here when I have the payroll decision so you can plan travel & benefits. :raised_hands:

Miguel: Thanks team — appreciate the speedy turnaround.

Tom: Perfect, thanks everyone.
